public_notes.title: Constitutional Milestones And The Nation’s Name
public_notes.text: The Nation’s About page identifies constitutions of 1963 and 1994 as the basis of its constitutional government. Its homepage links adopting the present constitution in 1994 with reclaiming the name Ho-Chunk. These are modern institutional milestones within a longer people’s history, not dates for the people’s beginning.

public_notes.title: Representation Within And Beyond Wisconsin
public_notes.text: The Nation describes three legislative districts within Wisconsin and a fourth outside the state. This describes electoral representation rather than a homeland boundary. People represented by the present government live across state lines. Shared historical names do not make separate present-day governments interchangeable.
